I’m sorry, but I don’t have a tool that can fetch holiday data from an external source. However, I can provide you with a list of the Canadian public holidays that typically create long weekends in 2023. You can then cross‑check these dates with your local holiday calendar or an official government source to confirm the exact long‑weekend dates for your province or territory.

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Typical Long‑Weekend Impact |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | January 1 (Sunday) | New Year’s Eve (Dec 31) + New Year’s Day (Jan 1) → 3‑day weekend |
| Family Day (BC, AB, SK, NB, PE) | February 20 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Feb 18‑20) |
| Louis Riel Day (MB) | February 20 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Feb 18‑20) |
| St. Patrick’s Day (NL) | March 17 (Friday) | 3‑day weekend (Mar 17‑19) |
| Good Friday | April 7 (Friday) | 3‑day weekend (Apr 7‑9) |
| Easter Monday (Ontario, PE) | April 10 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Apr 8‑10) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (May 20‑22) |
| Canada Day | July 1 (Saturday) | 3‑day weekend (Jun 30‑Jul 2) |
| Civic Holiday (BC, NB, PE, SK, MB) | August 7 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Aug 5‑7) |
| Labour Day | September 4 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Sep 2‑4) |
| Thanksgiving (Canada) | October 9 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Oct 7‑9) |
| Remembrance Day | November 11 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Nov 9‑11) |
| Christmas Day | December 25 (Monday) | 3‑day weekend (Dec 23‑25) |
| Boxing Day | December 26 (Tuesday) | 3‑day weekend (Dec 24‑26) |

**Notes**

* Some provinces/territories observe additional holidays (e.g., **St. John’s Day** in Newfoundland & Labrador, **National Indigenous Peoples Day** in Yukon, etc.) that may also create long weekends.
* If a holiday falls on a weekend, the statutory holiday is often observed on the following Monday, which can shift the long‑weekend window.
* For the most accurate planning, verify the holiday dates for each province/territory you’re interested in, as the above table lists only the federal holidays that are common across Canada.

If you need a more detailed, province‑specific list or a programmatic way to retrieve the dates, you might consider using a holiday‑API service (e.g., **Calendarific**, **Date.nager.at**, or a local government API) and then integrating that data into your app.
